title: handsets.toml — the hardware inventory
description: The phone plant: what physically exists. `doorman render` generates the per-handset Asterisk config from this file, so ids, endpoints, and dialplan cannot drift apart. Changes when you buy hardware. Rules live in policy.toml.

groups.description: Named sets of handsets, usable anywhere a handset id is.

x-rules: May not collide with any handset id.

handsets.description: Every physical phone or dialplan destination.

endpoint.description: Asterisk endpoint. Must be PJSIP/<id> — `doorman render` enforces the match so the generated config cannot disagree with the inventory.

x-rules: Must be unique across handsets and groups.

label.description: Human name, shown in `doorman check` output.

mailbox.description: Mailbox whose message-waiting lamp this phone follows.

number.description: Internal extension for handset-to-handset dialling and BLF hints. 0 or absent means not directly dialable.
x-rules: Two handsets may not share a number.
0 is allowed and means not dialable.

page.description: Include in the page-all group reached by dialling 500.

password_env.description: Name of the .env variable holding this handset's SIP password. The secret itself never appears in this file. `doorman render` substitutes it and fails if unset.
x-rules: Required by `doorman render`, which reports it as an error when missing.
Names a variable; never put the password here.
At least one [[handsets]] entry is required.
A group id may appear anywhere a handset id may, and expands at load time.
Groups may contain handsets only, never other groups — no cycles.
